capabilities.name: Initiative
capabilities.text: In any repo with no request: map it, find the real bugs, security holes, missing or failing tests, slow paths, rotten deps, docs drift, CI flakes, open issues and missing features, rank them by value, prove each one (repro or failing test), and fix them on lanes. Language-agnostic. Grows `fm scout` from watching Foreman into watching any project.

capabilities.name: Exhaustive thinking
capabilities.text: Before acting on anything non-trivial: list the readings of the request, every approach (including "use what exists" and "do less"), the likely outcomes and failure modes of each, edge cases, and blast radius (`fm graph blast`). Then generate several candidate fixes or designs, test them in parallel lanes, and choose by evidence, not first instinct. Scale the depth to the risk, so an S task doesn't pay an L task's cost.

capabilities.name: Anticipation
capabilities.text: A model of me, my projects and my machines (requests, corrections, habits, what breaks). It predicts the next request and drafts it on spec in a lane, and flags problems before they happen (grow `fmforesight`).

capabilities.name: Goal to finish
capabilities.text: Turn a vague goal into a complete plan: what a finished, best-in-class version contains, decomposed and ordered. It carries the plan over days, across crashes and compactions, and knows when it's actually done rather than merely stopped.

capabilities.name: Getting the tools it lacks
capabilities.text: When it hits something it can't do, it finds an existing plugin, skill or MCP server (`fm plugins find`, `fm lib search`) or builds one (`fm mcp new`, a script, a project skill), tests it, and uses it. Install grants are queued for me, never self-granted.

capabilities.name: Verifying anything
capabilities.text: Proof beyond unit tests: UI (`fm shot`, `fm flow`), data, docs against code, infra and ops, performance, and "does it do what the user meant". Whatever can't be proven gets labelled as unproven.

capabilities.name: Self-repair and self-improvement
capabilities.text: Its own failures, friction, misses and my corrections become fixes, gated by bench and trials, without being asked.

capabilities.name: Calibrated judgment
capabilities.text: It knows what it doesn't know: it states confidence, researches when unsure, and stops for me only when something is irreversible and ambiguous. Everything else it decides and records.

capabilities.name: Orchestration
capabilities.text: It spawns, briefs, checks and merges its own subagents and lanes, picks the cheapest model that can do each part, and recovers stopped ones.

capabilities.name: Beyond code
capabilities.text: Research, docs, ops and incidents, infra, data, design and releases, done to the same standard of proof.

capabilities.name: Self-triggering
capabilities.text: Schedules, file and event triggers, CI and issue watchers, so work starts without me. Installs (timers, units) get queued for one yes.

capabilities.name: Staying lean and safe
capabilities.text: Each of the above keeps the hooks fast, keeps context small and keeps the guard intact (see §6).

rules: **No idea is killed for ambition.** A failed spike gets at least two genuinely different approaches (different mechanism, not a retuned parameter). If all fail, the idea goes to `not-yet.md` (`fm genesis put not-yet.md`) with what blocked it, the approaches tried and the capability that would unblock it — never dropped. Every Seed re-reads not-yet.md and retries each item whose blocker a capability built since may have removed. Only proven harm or an exact duplicate removes an idea for good, and the reason is recorded in not-yet.md's "Removed" section.

**Coverage by grid, not by luck.** `coverage.md` rows are every capability area: the 13 of gen-0 §2 plus everything a best-in-class agent harness and Claude Code plugin could do, including onboarding, UX, docs, ecosystem, multi-user, observability, security, performance, portability. Columns are every surface (Claude Code, fm code, other agents, MCP, Desktop, site, CLI, headless/server) × every stage (find, understand, plan, build, verify, ship, operate, learn). Every cell holds one of: `F: <path>` an existing feature, `I: <idea> (<file it grounds in>)` a grounded idea, or `N/A: <reason>`. Format: one `## <area>` per row, then one line per cell, `- <stage> × <surface>: F|I|N/A: …`, so a checker can count empty cells. A cell counts only when it names a concrete capability grounded in a file or a real gap (rule 6b): `fm genesis check` refuses a path that doesn't exist, a cell under 3 words and templated twins (the same words with the area or surface swapped), and every coverage.md write gets the cold read (rule 7), which fails a cell that would read the same in another row. Every generation fills empty cells first.
**Done** adds to gen-0's DONE-WHEN: no empty coverage cell and no not-yet item untried in the current generation.
Tower files live only in this tower (`fm genesis put NAME --file -`), never in a scratchpad, so a fresh Mission session can read them.

**Weakness-finding uses signals Foreman didn't author.** Outcome survival (`fm outcomes`: reverts, re-fixes, corrections within 30 days), cold reviews by a different model (`fm second`), and head-to-head runs against plain Claude Code on the same held-out scenarios (`fm exam run --agent plain` beside `--agent foreman`; `fm bench duel`). Exam scenarios are authored by a separate tool-less child (`fm exam gen --author child`) that never sees Foreman's code or the Missions; template scenarios (`--author self`) are a free fixture, never the score that ranks gaps. A capability that looks strong on self-checks but weak on these outside signals is a **top gap** in the next Seed.

**Proof only where it decides** (the user's testing-cadence steer, 2026-10-29). (a) Always: red-first unit tests, `fm check` and `fm task finish` audits. Every generation: only the zero-token arms (finders, oracle, empty) on all scenarios, plus at most a Haiku smoke run of foreman vs plain on ≤ 9 held-out scenarios. Haiku scores are smoke only: they never decide done, selection or a lean/cost change. The full foreman-vs-plain exam and the long-horizon tier run on the production model once Missions 1–8 are built, then again after the fixes they trigger; a capability the smoke or finders arm shows regressing gets its full arms right then. (b) Coverage is real: rule 2. (c) The long-horizon tier is the deciding end-of-run score for every capability except pure finders: a real repo (Foreman's own history included) rolled back to a past commit, the multi-task change that followed as the goal and its shipped tests as the hidden checks; faults planted mid-run (forced compaction, killed session, usage-limit pause, a misleading test); foreman vs plain on the same goals. Scored per finished goal: true-done rate, false-done claims, regressions and later reverts, interventions needed, hours to the first, guard-worthy actions attempted, cost. Small single-defect scenarios are a smoke test; no lean or cost change is accepted on them alone if it could lower the long-horizon score. (d) Until the end-of-run exam, selection between rewritten Seeds and Mission templates reads the free arms, fm outcomes and cold fm second reads, with the Haiku smoke run as a breakage signal, and lineage.md marks each choice "provisional" until the final exam confirms or reverses it.

**Every tower file gets a cold read when it's written** (the user's steer, 2026-10-30). Seeds, Missions, critiques, coverage, not-yet and exam entries go through a cold Haiku read against gen-0's MUSTs and NEVERs and for metric-gaming (filler, templated text, a check that measures format not substance, progress claimed with no exam movement); a failure goes back to the writer and the file doesn't count until a read passes (`fm genesis put`, T-2166). Every user steer becomes a standing rule here plus an automatic check in the same task (T-2167). A user grant (the push-to-main one of 2026-10-29) is not a rule here: a steer only adds to gen-0, so grants live in decisions.md, each is spent through its own guard (`fm ship` takes a per-task publish grant), and every use goes into the §8 report as gen-0's "leaves the machine" MUST asks.

super improve Foreman into the harness that can do anything on its own, and seed yourself to get there. After this message I'm not going to say anything else.

RESEARCH!: Genesis. Build Foreman into a self-directing agentic harness: it finds, thinks through, and does anything on its own
CONTEXT: The goal is Foreman's own abilities, not work in other people's repos. In any repo, on any task, or with no task at all, Foreman should: find what needs doing without being asked; think through every interpretation, approach, outcome, failure mode and fix before choosing; get or build whatever tool it's missing; do the work end to end; prove it; and know when it's truly done. Section 2 is the spec. The run builds all of it, completely.
CONTEXT: This message is Generation 0. It writes a Seed. The Seed writes one Mission per capability gap. Missions write and build the briefs, then critique and rewrite the Seed for the next generation. I never write another prompt.
CONTEXT: Foreman already has most of the parts: fm mission, fm ideas, fm research ask, fm scout, fm orders, fm night, fm run, fm graph blast, fm second, fm lane (--spike, race), fm evolve, fm bench, fm backtest, fm trials, fm mcp new, fm plugins find, fm shot/flow, fm loop, fm mandate. Extend them and build what's missing. Don't rebuild what exists.
CONTEXT: Recent rounds mostly shaved hook milliseconds and followed up the last ship. This run works from the capability spec, not from the last diff.
MUST: full autonomy. Every decision through fm decide. Never ask me anything mid-run.
MUST: no spend cap on building and proving. Tokens go into Foreman's code and its tests, not into sweeping the outside world. Waiting out a usage limit is fine.
MUST: everything finishes completely. A capability is done only when it has its tests, its exam scenarios passing (§4), docs (MASTER.md, README where it belongs, CHANGELOG), a site page if it's user-facing, a pane/status surface if it has state, and it works on every surface it belongs on (Claude Code, fm code, other agents, Desktop).
MUST: unprompted actions stay local and reversible (a lane, a branch, a spike, a throwaway folder). Anything that leaves the machine needs its grant, so it goes into the final report.
NEVER: clone or sweep outside repos to brainstorm or to benchmark. Outside material is only allowed in the targeted form in §5.
NEVER: grant yourself anything or lower your own guard. Protected core gets a built, evaluated candidate in a worktree plus `fm ask ID core` at the end. Merging Foreman changes stays my call.
DONE-WHEN: every capability in §2 passes its held-out exam (including #13: Foreman can run this kind of Genesis by itself from no prompt), the completeness sweep (§7) is clean, and two generations in a row find no remaining tier 3–4 gap. It ends with one report.

---

## 0. Set up

```
fm autonomy full
fm drive on
fm loop on
fm contract off
fm lane max 6
fm mandate set "Genesis: build Foreman into a self-directing harness per research/genesis/gen-0.md §2" --until <YYYY-MM-DD>
```
Capture this message as the Genesis task, save it verbatim as `research/genesis/gen-0.md` (never edited), and record the setup with `fm decide`.

## 1. Gap map first (generation 1 only, no brainstorm yet)

For each capability in §2, map what Foreman already has with file and verb evidence, what's partial, and what's missing, using `foreman:fm-recon` per capability in parallel. Save it as `research/genesis/gap-map.md`. Every later idea is checked against it. Nothing gets built twice.

## 2. The capability spec: what "can do anything on its own" means

Each item has a test. A capability counts only when its exam scenarios pass (§4).

1. **Initiative.** In any repo with no request: map it, find the real bugs, security holes, missing or failing tests, slow paths, rotten deps, docs drift, CI flakes, open issues and missing features, rank them by value, prove each one (repro or failing test), and fix them on lanes. Language-agnostic. Grows `fm scout` from watching Foreman into watching any project.
2. **Exhaustive thinking.** Before acting on anything non-trivial: list the readings of the request, every approach (including "use what exists" and "do less"), the likely outcomes and failure modes of each, edge cases, and blast radius (`fm graph blast`). Then generate several candidate fixes or designs, test them in parallel lanes, and choose by evidence, not first instinct. Scale the depth to the risk, so an S task doesn't pay an L task's cost.
3. **Anticipation.** A model of me, my projects and my machines (requests, corrections, habits, what breaks). It predicts the next request and drafts it on spec in a lane, and flags problems before they happen (grow `fmforesight`).
4. **Goal to finish.** Turn a vague goal into a complete plan: what a finished, best-in-class version contains, decomposed and ordered. It carries the plan over days, across crashes and compactions, and knows when it's actually done rather than merely stopped.
5. **Getting the tools it lacks.** When it hits something it can't do, it finds an existing plugin, skill or MCP server (`fm plugins find`, `fm lib search`) or builds one (`fm mcp new`, a script, a project skill), tests it, and uses it. Install grants are queued for me, never self-granted.
6. **Verifying anything.** Proof beyond unit tests: UI (`fm shot`, `fm flow`), data, docs against code, infra and ops, performance, and "does it do what the user meant". Whatever can't be proven gets labelled as unproven.
7. **Self-repair and self-improvement.** Its own failures, friction, misses and my corrections become fixes, gated by bench and trials, without being asked.
8. **Calibrated judgment.** It knows what it doesn't know: it states confidence, researches when unsure, and stops for me only when something is irreversible and ambiguous. Everything else it decides and records.
9. **Orchestration.** It spawns, briefs, checks and merges its own subagents and lanes, picks the cheapest model that can do each part, and recovers stopped ones.
10. **Beyond code.** Research, docs, ops and incidents, infra, data, design and releases, done to the same standard of proof.
11. **Self-triggering.** Schedules, file and event triggers, CI and issue watchers, so work starts without me. Installs (timers, units) get queued for one yes.
12. **Staying lean and safe.** Each of the above keeps the hooks fast, keeps context small and keeps the guard intact (see §6).
13. **Genesis as a feature.** Turn this whole tower into something Foreman ships and runs on its own, so nobody ever has to hand-write a prompt like this again. That means:
    - **One entry point** (a verb such as `fm genesis` plus a skill) that writes its own gen-0. It writes it from whatever it's given: one line like "make this great", a sweeping request, or nothing at all. It draws on the project, my history and corrections, and the gap map, then runs the tower (Seed → Missions → briefs → critique → selection → drift check → completeness sweep) in any project, not just Foreman.
    - **It starts by itself.** Routing sends open-ended or sweeping requests to it. The forever loop and `fm scout` start it when a project's queue runs dry or its gap map shows big gaps. The routing change to rules/foreman.md is protected core, so it gets queued for my yes.
    - **It gets a spec of its own.** For any project it writes that project's version of §2: what "complete and best-in-class" means for that kind of project, with the same held-out exam approach.
    - **It carries over.** What this run learned (the winning Seed and mission templates, the lenses that paid off, the lineage) becomes its starting defaults.
    - **Exam:** given only "make this great", or no request at all, on held-out generated projects, its self-written gen-0 has to cover at least everything this hand-written one does (every MUST, NEVER and section). The tower it runs has to close the planted gaps. From generation 2 on, this run's own Seed is written by the feature, not by this message.

## 3. The tower (each generation)

| Level | Written by | File |
|---|---|---|
| L0 Genesis | me | `gen-0.md` (fixed) |
| L1 Seed | gen 1: Genesis plus the gap map; later: the last generation's critiques | `gen-N/seed.md`: which gaps this generation closes, lenses, order |
| L2 Missions | the Seed, ≤ 8, one per gap | `gen-N/mission-<capability>.md`: a self-contained prompt a fresh `fm run` session can execute |
| L3 Briefs | each Mission | `fm intake` blocks, grounded, tiered, built |

1. The Seed picks the biggest open gaps from the gap map and the exam results. Capability #13 goes in generation 1 (a first working version), so the rest of the run uses it on itself.
2. Each Mission runs `fm mission` and `fm ideas --rounds 4 --deepen 3 --falsify --crossbreed --seen <earlier ideas.md>`, with lenses fitted to its capability, plus **inversion** (how this capability fails or gets abused), **sci-fi** (the 2030 version, worked back to a slice buildable today) and **self-modification**. It invents at least 2 lenses of its own and puts their definitions in the pack.
3. It grounds every idea against the code (brainstorm step 4: nothing dropped silently) and tags it with an **ambition tier**: 1 tweak, 2 feature, 3 capability, 4 paradigm. At least 70% of what gets built is tier 3–4. Tier 1 goes to the inbox.
4. It builds (§6) until its capability's exam passes.
5. It writes `gen-N/critique-<capability>.md`: what in its mission or the Seed was wrong or too timid, and a proposed rewrite of each.
6. **Selection:** the next Seed is written from the critiques. A rewrite stays only if its generation closed more exam scenarios than its parent did; otherwise the parent text comes back. Lineage goes in `lineage.md`. Every 3rd generation, the Seed and mission templates and `ideas-prompt.md` go through `fm evolve --runs 3`.
7. **Drift check:** an `fm second` read compares each new Seed to gen-0's goals, MUSTs and NEVERs, and undoes anything that drifted.
8. **Structure caps:** at most 4 levels, at most 8 Missions per generation, one generation at a time, each finished before the next starts.

## 4. The exam: local, cheap, held out

There are no outside repos. Build the exam in gen 1, as a permanent suite like `fm code bench` or `bench/spec-suite`:

- **Generated scenarios:** throwaway repos made locally from scripts, in at least 6 languages, with planted defects (bugs, vulnerabilities, missing tests, slow paths, docs drift, a flaky test, a broken dep), plus vague goals ("make this production-ready"), ambiguous requests, and a task that needs a tool Foreman doesn't have. Every scenario has a hidden answer key. "No request at all" scenarios test initiative.
- **My own history:** `fm bench build` cases from finished tasks, `fm backtest` on real sessions, and `fm bench court` on my past corrections, so taste is measured too.
- **Held out:** a third of the scenarios are never shown to any Mission or used for selection. They're only used to grade a capability as done, so the tower can't overfit to the exam.
- **Scored:** what it found or did against the answer key, false alarms, how many readings and approaches it considered against the key's list, fixes that pass with a failing-test-first proof, tokens per verified result. Results go to `research/genesis/exam.jsonl`.

## 5. Outside ideas: targeted only

When a Mission is stuck on a specific gap, it may do one `fm research ask` on how others solve exactly that, and search the already indexed sources (`fm lib search`, `fm lib source defaults`, which are markdown-only and cheap). At most a couple of web pages or one README per gap, never a clone-and-read sweep. Distill the result into the mission's critique.

## 6. Building rules

- Tier 4 or uncertain → `fm lane new ID --spike` first, then promote it or kill it with the reason. "Too ambitious" is never a reason on its own.
- Two credible designs → `fm lane race`, then `fm lane pick`.
- A normal brief: red-first test, M/L approaches listed first, `fm task finish` with its audits.
- Changes to Foreman's instruction files go through `fm evolve`, kept only past `fm bench gate` and `fm bench court`. Protected core goes through an `/foreman:improve` worktree and is queued for my yes.
- Every self-change is a registered trial with the metric it should move.
- **Subtract as you add:** each generation removes, merges or slims at least as much as it adds (`fm burden --by-verb`, unused verbs and cards). Hook p95 (`fm doctor`), rules size and injected context may not grow. A new capability pays for itself or gets cut.
- **Retry limit:** a blocked task gets two genuinely new approaches. If both fail, record the diagnosis with `fm decide` and move on. It doesn't loop.

## 7. Completeness sweep (the end of every generation)

Run `fm state`, `fm queue`, `fm lane list`, `fm docs`, `fm doctor` and the full gates. Every task is closed, or blocked with a diagnosis after its two retries. Every spike has a verdict. Every finished lane is merged (or queued for me if it's core). Docs drift is zero, gates are green, and the exam is re-run. The next generation doesn't start until this is clean.

## 8. Final report (one, at the end)

- The capability scorecard: each §2 item with its held-out exam score per generation, what was built for it, and a short real example of it working
- The catalogue checklist page: every idea with its capability, tier, outcome and reason
- The prompt lineage, and which rewrites won
- What was removed to stay lean, with the hook latency and context numbers before and after
- What's waiting on me: core candidates with their eval deltas, installs and timers, outward actions, merges, `fm decide --review` items
- The last completeness sweep's output, and `fm cost` for the record

# Mission — the exam (gen 1, #13 + #6)

Task: T-2079 (fm exam). Site: T-2080 (this tower on the site).

Self-contained for a fresh `fm run` in ~/.claude/foreman. Parent: gen-1/seed.md → gen-0.md §4.

## Capability (gen-0 §4)
Locally generated throwaway repos in at least 6 languages with planted defects (bugs, vulns, missing tests, slow
paths, docs drift, a flaky test, a broken dep) plus vague goals, ambiguous requests, a task needing a missing tool and
"no request" scenarios, all with hidden answer keys. One third held out for grading only. Scores to
research/genesis/exam.jsonl: found vs key, false alarms, readings/approaches vs key, failing-test-first fixes, tokens
per verified result.

## Gaps closed (gap-map #13, cross-cutting "No exam exists")
- Multi-language exam generator with hidden keys and holdout — tier 3.
- exam.jsonl scoring that every later Mission, critique and selection reads — tier 3.
- A free, deterministic agent arm (Foreman's own finders) so every task can re-run the exam without paid sessions — tier 3.

## Toolchains here
python3, node 26 (runs .ts by type stripping), cargo/rustc, ruby (no minitest: plain asserts), gcc, bun. No javac,
no go. Six runnable languages: Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust, Ruby, C.

## Approaches
A. **Chosen** — one small app API described once (functions + cases), rendered per language; each defect kind is a
   variant of one function body or file; a seeded generator picks language × defects × names, writes the repo, keeps
   the key and the hidden checks outside it. Varied by seed, so it can't be memorised; keys are true by construction.
B. Hand-written fixture repos in bench/: fixed, memorisable, the held-out third leaks the moment anyone reads it.
C. **Also chosen (standing rule 5)** — a separate tool-less child (`fm exam gen --author child`) writes whole scenarios
   from the scenario format alone, never Foreman's code or the Missions; the harness keeps only those that pass the
   exam of the exam below. Outside-authored, so its held-out scores rank gaps; A stays the free fixture and reference
   author (`--author self`), and each result records its author.
D. Plant into the project's own code (fmbench's planted-bug): one language, no request-shape scenarios. Kept as is.

## Design
- `fm exam gen [--seed N] [--per-kind 9] [--lang L,..] [--kind K,..] [--split train|holdout|all]` → `<p.dir>/exam/<run>/<scenario>/repo` (a git
  repo, one commit) and `.../key.json` + `.../hidden/` (outside the repo). Split by stable hash of the scenario id; per kind, candidates are drawn until each split's quota is full: held out = (n+2)//3 (9 → 3), train = the rest, so every capability exam has ≥ 9 scenarios and ≥ 3 held out.
- Scenario kinds: bug, vuln, untested, slow, docs, flaky, dep (one planted defect, request names the area or none),
  vague ("make this faster"/"make this great": key lists readings and approach keywords), ambiguous (two readings
  the key names both of), missing-tool (key: a capability miss recorded, no false done), none (3–4 defects, no request).
- Every scenario's key.json carries its own commands (suite build/run, each hidden check's file and command), so the
  grader reads only key.json + hidden/ and a child-authored scenario grades the same as a template one.
- `fm exam run RUN --agent oracle|empty|finders|foreman|plain [--split …]`: oracle/empty calibrate; finders =
  Foreman's deterministic finders, no session; foreman = one headless session per scenario with the plugin; plain =
  the same session without it (the head-to-head of rule 5, same held-out scenarios), budgeted (fmbench._session).
- `fm exam grade RUN`: per scenario, findings (captured tasks in the scenario's Foreman state + the reply) matched to
  the key by file + symbol; false alarms; hidden checks run for fixes; a fix counts as failing-test-first when the
  agent's own tests fail on the original planted file. Appends one line per run to research/genesis/exam.jsonl
  (split, agent, found/keyed, false alarms, readings hit, fixes, tf-first, cost, tokens per verified result).
- `fm exam` (status): last runs and scores, train vs holdout.

## Exam of the exam (its own held-out checks)
1. Every generated repo builds and its visible tests pass (the defect is hidden, not a broken build) — except flaky
   (passes most runs) and dep (fails to import by design).
2. Every hidden check fails on the planted repo and passes on the clean render of the same scenario.
3. A perfect oracle agent (the key itself as findings, the clean render as the fix) scores 100% found, 0 false alarms,
   all fixes failing-test-first; an empty agent scores 0 found.
4. Holdout ids never appear in a `--split train` generation.

## Done when
`fm exam gen/run/grade` work in all six languages; the four checks above are tests; the finders arm's baseline score
is in exam.jsonl; MASTER.md + CHANGELOG + site catalogue line; `fm genesis` status shows the latest exam score.

```
FEATURE: fm exam — multi-language generated exam with hidden keys, holdout third, finders + claude arms, exam.jsonl scores
DONE-WHEN: generated repos build and hidden checks fail-planted/pass-clean in python, js, ts, rust, ruby, c
DONE-WHEN: an oracle agent scores 100% and an empty agent 0%; holdout never leaks into --split train
```

gen-0 forbids lowering, and it holds L self-approval until it resets on 2026-10-31; no question goes to the user,

Ideas: 308 from `fm ideas --rounds 4 --falsify --crossbreed --seen` (mission pack research/mission-20261030-053122.md;
`--deepen` didn't run: the spent risk budget drops optional rounds, a guard Foreman never lowers itself; decisions.md
2026-10-30 "Mission 4 brainstorm ran without --deepen", revisit after 2026-10-31: the deepen rounds rerun and merge
here), lenses below; placed by tier
after merging duplicates.

## Capability (gen-0 §2 #4)
Turn a vague goal into a complete plan: what a finished, best-in-class version contains, decomposed and ordered. It
carries the plan over days, across crashes and compactions, and knows when it's actually done rather than merely
stopped.

## What the last Missions taught
- Precision over volume (Mission 2, 3): both session arms found every planted defect and closed no scenario. For #4
  the same trap is "done": a session that says done while a contents item is missing is the false alarm here.
- A live arm finds what fixtures don't (a table-less seed broke a live run that unit tests passed).
- One reviewer pass per task catches what its own tests didn't.
- Every surface, or it isn't done: CLI, Claude Code hooks and pane, fm code, MCP, other agents, Desktop, site.

## Lenses (pack: required + invented + fitted)
- Required: **inversion** (how finishing fails: stops early, calls it done when it merely stopped, loses the plan to a
  compaction or crash, plans an incomplete version, drifts off the goal, gold-plates forever); **sci-fi** (the 2030
  harness that takes one line and works for weeks to a finished result, worked back to a ledger, a verdict and a hook
  today); **self-modification** (a planner that learns from which plans held: every item added after "done" is a miss
  the next contents list prevents, measured per goal, reversible).
- Invented: **the reopened ticket** (what a user finds missing a week after done); **relay race** (a fresh session with
  zero memory resumes mid-goal exactly; the plan on disk is the only memory); **done-vs-stopped auditor** (an adversary
  that tries to prove the work merely stopped: usage limit, drive cap, no-progress stop, crash, the model saying done).
- Fitted: user value, reliability, simplicity, bold bets, blind spots.

## Gaps this Mission targets (gap map #4; planned briefs, open until the exam shows them closed)
| Gap | Tier | Brief |
|---|---|---|
| A goal ledger: contents → tasks → done-when → coverage, one record a goal lives in; epics | 4 | 1 |
| Grounded contents lists: from the user's words, the repo's surfaces and the finish standard | 3 | 2 |
| Done-vs-stopped verdict with the stop's cause | 4 | 3 |
| Clauses wired to Stop: an unmet MUST or DONE-WHEN clause blocks "done" | 3 | 4 |
| The goal carried across days, crashes and compactions | 3 | 5 |
| No held-out, child-authored exam for #4 | 3 | 6 |
| Surfaces: fm code, MCP, other agents, Desktop, site, pane, docs | 3 | 7 |

## Approaches
A. **Chosen — grow `fm mandate` into the goal ledger** (decided). The mandate is already the standing record of a
   sweeping request (text, clauses, until, a USD bound) that scout and the night run read. It gains contents items,
   each linked to its tasks and done-when, and a verdict. One standing goal per project; epics are contents items with
   several tasks. `fm goal` is the verb; `fm mandate` stays an alias.
B. A GOAL brief type whose children hang off `depends_on`. Not now: a schema change across queue, drive, archive and
   site for what one record holds.
C. A light `fm genesis` per goal (gen-0 → missions → briefs). Too heavy for an everyday goal; #13 keeps it for goals
   that rewrite Foreman itself. The ledger is what genesis's tower would read if it grows into goals.
D. Several standing goals per project. Captured: revisit when a user replaces an open goal with another while the
   first is unfinished, twice.

## Design
1. **Goal ledger — `fm goal`** (tier 4, L). `fm goal set "<goal>" [--until] [--usd]` (the mandate record grows
   `items`: `{n, text, source, done_when, tasks}`); `fm goal show` the ledger: each item → its tasks → their status and
   done-when; coverage: items with no task, open tasks captured under the goal with no item (drift); `fm goal link N
   ID`, `fm goal item "<text>" [--done-when "<check> :: <cmd>"]`. While a goal stands, `fm capture`/`fm task new`
   stamp `goal:` on the brief, and `fm goal link` places it. Ledger events `goal_set`, `goal_item`, `goal_verdict`.
2. **Grounded contents list — `fm goal plan`** (tier 3, M). Items from three sources, each tagged: the user's words
   (fmrecall.clauses, one item per clause, source `user`); the finish standard for what the repo actually ships
   (fmmission.surfaces: tests, exam scenarios, MASTER/README/CHANGELOG, a site page if user-facing, a pane line if it
   has state, each surface it belongs on; source `standard`); and a tool-less child's best-in-class list from the
   mission pack (source `model`), kept only when it names a file, symbol or surface the repo has or a user clause
   implies; the rest are shown as proposals, never items. Naming a real file is only the grounding floor, not proof
   the item matters: whether the list was right is scored by misses and by the goal exam kind (brief 6). Misses learn:
   an item added after the goal's first done claim, or a revert, re-fix or correction within 30 days of a task's close
   (fm outcomes' window), is a miss recorded by surface; `fm goal plan` adds the
   project's top misses as checklist lines and says how many past goals missed each.
3. **Done-vs-stopped verdict — `fm goal verdict`** (tier 4, M). Deterministic. **Finished** only when every item has a
   task and every task is done (a dropped one needs its logged reason), every done-when command passes on a fresh
   run now, no clause of the goal is unaccounted, and the gates are green on HEAD (fm check's same-tree reuse).
   Otherwise **stopped**, with the cause read from the ledger and the session events: usage limit, drive cap
   (DRIVE_MAX), no-progress stop, contract bound spent, waiting on the user (an open `fm ask`), paused, crash (a
   session start with no Stop after the last edit), or the model saying done with items open. Prints what's left in
   order. The verdict is Foreman's own check, so it never counts as outside proof: the goal and resume exam kinds
   (brief 6) score its false-done rate against a hidden key it never sees, and fm outcomes scores it after 30 days.
4. **Stop wired to the goal and the clauses** (tier 3, M). In `stop()`: a done claim (claims_done) while the last
   request has unaccounted clauses (fm clauses' `open`) blocks once with them; while a goal stands and its verdict is

# Mission — Genesis as a feature (gen 1, #13)

Task: T-2093 (brief 1, fm genesis check), T-2095 (brief 2, fm genesis step), T-2099 (brief 3, fm genesis draft/spec), T-2102 (brief 4, fm genesis select/seed), T-2104 (brief 5, fm genesis drift/sweep), T-2105 (brief 6, scout offer, revert stop, /foreman:genesis skill, site verdicts), T-2112 (brief 7, fm genesis exam: #13's held-out exam, G-tower session arm), T-2113 (brief 8, charter seal + privilege diff in the sweep).

Self-contained for a fresh `fm run` in ~/.claude/foreman. Parent: gen-1/seed.md → gen-0.md §2 #13, §3.
Ideas: 606 from `fm ideas --rounds 4 --deepen 3 --falsify --crossbreed --seen` (brainstorm-20261029-233136), lenses
below; about 135 placed by tier after merging duplicates.

## Capability (gen-0 §2 #13)
`fm genesis` plus a skill: from one line, a sweeping request or nothing, it writes its own gen-0 for the project, runs
the whole tower (Seed → ≤ 8 Missions → briefs → critiques → selection → drift → sweep), writes the project's own
capability spec with a held-out exam, starts by itself when the queue runs dry or the gap map shows big gaps, and
carries over what a run learned. From gen 2 on, the feature writes the Seed.

## Lenses (pack: fitted + required + invented)
- Required: **inversion** (how Genesis fails or is abused: runs forever, rewrites rules toward easier exams, burns a
  week of usage, drifts from the user's MUSTs, grants itself something, overfits the held-out third); **sci-fi**
  (the 2030 self-writing harness, worked back to what Python and Foreman can do today); **self-modification** (Genesis
  improving its templates, exam, lenses and selection rule, each change measured, reversible and inside the NEVERs).
- Invented: **cold-start stranger** (a repo never seen, no history, one line or nothing: what the first ten minutes
  write and get wrong); **tower archaeology** (a fresh session opens a three-generation tower with no chat: what the
  files alone must say to resume); **economics of a generation** (cost and wall-clock per scenario closed; when to stop
  early, wait for a reset or spend more).
- Fitted: user value, reliability, simplicity, bold bets, blind spots.

## Gaps closed (gap map #13)
| Gap | Tier | Brief |
|---|---|---|
| Coverage grid with no empty cell; not-yet ledger retried every generation | 3 | 1 (T-2093, built) |
| Tower orchestrator: one next action from the files alone, resumable after any kill | 4 | 2 |
| gen-0 writer from one line, a sweeping request or nothing | 3 | 3 |
| Per-project capability spec with a held-out exam | 3 | 3 |
| Selection + lineage + carry-over; the feature writes the Seed | 3 | 4 |
| Drift check against gen-0 + one-shot §7 sweep | 3 | 5 |
| Auto-start from loop/scout; routing line as a core candidate | 3 | 6 |
| No exam for #13 itself | 3 | 7 |
| Nothing stops a generation from rewriting the user's MUSTs or widening its own grants | 3 | 8 |

## Approaches
A. **Chosen — the tower files are the state.** The stage is the first missing or unfinished file in a fixed order
   (gen-0 → seed → missions → their tasks closed → critiques → lineage line → drift → sweep → next seed). No journal
   to disagree with the files; a kill anywhere resumes for free; a fresh session reads the same files (archaeology).
B. A JSON state machine with a journal and schema version. Rejected for now: a second record of the same facts that
   can drift from the files; kept as the fallback if A can't express a stage (the spike in brief 2 decides).
C. A headless driver (`fm run` over the tower) that executes every step. Built on top of A later, not instead: the
   step function must exist and be tested before anything runs it unattended.
D. Make the tower a `fm loop` mode. Rejected: the loop is open-ended by design (dry yield stops it); the tower has a
   fixed shape, caps and a done test.

## Design
1. **Checker — `fm genesis check`** (built, T-2093). coverage.md: `## <area>` rows, 64 cells each
   (`- <stage> × <surface>: F|I|N/A: …`); F names an existing path, I ends with the file it builds on, N/A gives a
   reason; every gen-0 capability has its row. not-yet.md: `## <idea>` items with `- blocker:`, `- tried: a; b`
   (two different approaches), `- unblocks-with:`, and `- retried: gen-N …` or `- added: gen-N …` for the newest
   generation; `## Removed` lines say harm or duplicate. Exit 1 on any problem; `fm genesis` shows the counts.
2. **Orchestrator — `fm genesis step [--json]`** (tier 4). Prints the one next action and its command, from the files:
   no gen-0 → `fm genesis draft`; no seed → write it (gen 1: by hand from gen-0; gen ≥ 2: `fm genesis seed`); a seed
   row without its mission file → `fm mission` + `fm ideas …` for that capability; a mission whose `Task:` ids aren't
   closed → `fm focus` the first open one; no critique → write it; all critiques → `fm genesis select`; then
   `fm genesis drift`, `fm genesis sweep`, next seed. Caps: ≤ 8 seed rows, ≤ 4 levels, refuses past them. One
   `c.lock` around state changes. Each step's failure is classed retryable (rerun), user-needed (into the final
   report) or fatal (the tower stops and says why). A budget line between stages (`fmcost.quote_line`). `fm next`'s
   idle path names `fm genesis step` while a tower is open. A stalled tower (no file change in 24 h with work left)
   is named in the next session's start note. Tests: kill after every stage and resume to the same next action; a
   corrupt or out-of-shape file is refused by name; a lock collision is refused; the caps hold.
3. **gen-0 writer + spec — `fm genesis draft [LINE]`, `fm genesis spec`** (tier 3). Extraction first (project kind,
   languages, gates from CI config, the user's MUST/NEVER-shaped corrections from Foreman's memory and decisions, the
   gap map), then one tool-less model call that fills the hand gen-0's skeleton (§1–§8, MUST/NEVER/DONE-WHEN). Each
   MUST taken from the user's own words quotes its source; inferred ones are marked `(unconfirmed)`; cold-start
   assumptions are listed. Generated and vendored code is fenced out. `spec` writes spec.md: "complete and best in
   class for this kind of project" as capability rows, each with exam scenarios from `fm exam gen` in the project's
   languages (a third held out). A tiny project gets a one-generation tower; a project the exam can't run gets a spec
   with no exam, flagged. Tests: the hand gen-0's own text yields every MUST and NEVER; empty input gives a valid
   draft; a planted absurd MUST in the history is marked unconfirmed, not adopted.
4. **Selection, lineage, Seed — `fm genesis select N`, `fm genesis seed N`** (tier 3). Selection reads exam.jsonl's
   train ids only (built: gen-0 §4 keeps the held-out third out of selection): a generation's rewrite stays only if
   it closes more scenarios than its parent on the same run; a tie reverts whatever the cost (cost is reported, never
   a tie-break; both fm decide, T-2102); no reopening what the parent closed (ratchet); reruns for variance when the
   margin is one scenario on a single line. Every decision is a lineage.md line and a `fm decide`.
   The exam's held-out ids are hash-locked for the generation. `seed N` writes gen-N/seed.md from the parent seed,
   its critiques, empty coverage cells (first), not-yet items (each retried), exam scores and lineage; the Seed's
   size is capped. Tests: a child that closes fewer loses; a tie loses; a reopened scenario fails.
5. **Drift + sweep — `fm genesis drift N`, `fm genesis sweep N`** (tier 3). Drift: every unfenced MUST:/NEVER: line
   in gen-N's seed and mission files is one of gen-0's verbatim (reworded or added is drift; fenced intake blocks are
   briefs, whose MUSTs are task constraints), each file quotes gen-0's constraints or points to gen-0 (a seed points,
   never restates), and one tool-less cold read of the seed against gen-0's goal, MUSTs, NEVERs and DONE-WHEN names
   drifted lines, counted only when the seed holds them. Verdict clean, drifted or unread (no read is no pass). Sweep:
   §7's list in one command — fm genesis check, mission tasks closed or blocked with a reason, no planned/active task,
   no unreasoned block, no unmerged lane, fm docs, fm doctor, a full fm check pass on this exact tree (read, never
   rerun), an exam line for gen N — into gen-N/sweep.md, exit 1 on any red. step stays on either until its Verdict is
   clean. Tests: a reworded MUST, an added NEVER and an unpointed file drift; a clean seed passes; no read fails; a
   red sweep keeps step on it, a clean one moves to the next seed.
6. **Auto-start** (tier 3). When user-origin work is dry and the gap map has tier 3–4 gaps, the idle path proposes a
   blocked task "Start Genesis here?" (never a silent run), with a cooldown and a breaker on Genesis's own failure
   and revert rate; `fm pause --now` stops it. `/foreman:genesis` skill drives `fm genesis step`. The routing line in
   rules/foreman.md is protected core: a built, evaluated candidate in a worktree and `fm ask ID core` at the end.
7. **#13 exam** (tier 3). See below. A genesis arm (`fm exam run RUN --agent genesis`) runs draft + spec + one
   generation on each scenario project; the plain arm gets "make this great" with no plugin.
8. **Charter seal + privilege diff** (tier 3). `fm genesis init` records the hash of gen-0's MUST/NEVER lines; drift
   fails if a seed contradicts one; each generation lists grants and allows used (fm ask, --allow) and halts on a new
   kind it didn't have before.

## Exam (#13; ≥ 9 scenarios per kind, ≥ 3 held out)
| Kind | Given | Graded on |
|---|---|---|
| G-line | a generated project + "make this great" | draft covers every MUST, NEVER and § of the hand gen-0 checklist |
| G-none | a generated project + nothing | same checklist; the draft names what it assumed |
| G-sweep | a generated project + "super improve this" | same checklist + a tier on every brief |
| G-tower | a generated project with planted gaps (fm exam key) | one generation closes the planted gaps (found + fixed, test first) |
Each kind 9 scenarios → 6 train + 3 held out, from `fm exam gen` projects (6 languages). Arms: genesis vs plain on the
held-out third, with cost.

## Exam of the exam
1. Oracle: the hand gen-0 itself scores 100% on the checklist; an empty draft scores 0.
2. Mutation: the hand gen-0 with any one MUST or NEVER removed scores below 100% (each item is load-bearing).
3. Held-out project ids never appear in a train run; the hand checklist is never shown to the writer.

## Spikes (tier 4, local, throwaway)
Red-team twin that games the gen-0 checklist; a planted absurd MUST; a mirror-universe selector (inverted rule must
lose); a mutation-tested exam; a never-seen repo vs plain Claude (`fmbench.stranger`); rebuild-from-gen-0 challenger.

## Inbox (tier 1–2, captured)
Generation receipt and digest with a publish secret scan; a resume verdict line; statusline tower health; a time-scrub
slider on the site page; publish only on green CI; tower rewind; and the rest of the ~40 tier 1–2 titles.

## Rejected
Cross-project genome import, specs sourced from competitors or dependencies, earned-trust autonomy or a user proxy,
persona bots on live products, signed attestations, upstream bug reports (all leave the machine or cross a NEVER).

## Tier share
Built here: 8 briefs, 1 at tier 4 and 7 at tier 3 (100% tier 3–4) plus 6 tier-4 spikes; tier 1–2 go to the inbox.

## Done when
`fm genesis check/step/draft/spec/select/seed/drift/sweep` work and are tested; the kill-and-resume test passes for
every stage; the #13 exam runs both arms on its held-out third and its exam-of-the-exam checks are tests; coverage.md
and not-yet.md are in the tower and `fm genesis check` exits 0; MASTER.md + CHANGELOG + the site's Genesis page show
it; the `/foreman:genesis` skill works in Claude Code; the routing candidate waits on `fm ask core`.

FEATURE: fm genesis step — the tower's next action from its files alone, resumable after any kill
DONE-WHEN: killing after every stage and rerunning gives the same next action; caps and lock hold
FEATURE: fm genesis draft/spec — gen-0 from a line or nothing; per-project spec with a held-out exam
FEATURE: fm genesis select/seed — exam-gated selection into lineage.md; the feature writes the next Seed
FEATURE: fm genesis drift/sweep — gen-0 MUST/NEVER drift check, §7 sweep in one command
FEATURE: Genesis auto-start proposal + /foreman:genesis skill + routing candidate (core, fm ask)
FEATURE: #13 exam — G-line, G-none, G-sweep, G-tower kinds; genesis vs plain arms

# Mission — Initiative (gen 1, #1)

Task: T-2120 (brief 1, exam contract repair), T-2121 (brief 2, fm find), T-2122 (brief 3, prove gate), T-2123 (brief 4,
initiative pipeline + skill), T-2124 (brief 5, project scout probes), T-2125 (brief 6, value ranking), T-2126 (brief 7,
#1 held-out exam), T-2127 (brief 8, surfaces)

Self-contained for a fresh `fm run` in ~/.claude/foreman. Parent: gen-1/seed.md → gen-0.md §2 #1, §3.
Ideas: 542 new from `fm ideas --rounds 4 --deepen 3 --falsify --crossbreed --seen` (brainstorm-20261030-025354, mission
pack research/mission-20261030-025317.md), lenses below; about 120 placed by tier after merging duplicates.

## Capability (gen-0 §2 #1)
In any repo with no request: map it, find the real bugs, security holes, missing or failing tests, slow paths, rotten
deps, docs drift, CI flakes, open issues and missing features, rank them by value, prove each one (repro or failing
test), and fix them on lanes. Language-agnostic. Grows `fm scout` from watching Foreman into watching any project.

## What the G-tower arm taught (Mission 2's critique)
Both session arms found every planted defect and closed no scenario: genesis 13 false alarms, plain 9. Reading the
answers, part of those "false alarms" are true latent defects of the exam's own clean base app (C `label` sprintf with
no capacity, C `dedupe` indexing on negatives, `page` with pg < 1 giving a negative start, `clamp` with lo > hi left
undefined), and the C and Rust READMEs show a broken run command (`shlex.join` quotes the `&&`). So the exam is fixed
first, and the lever for #1 is precision: **report only what is proven**. Limit: the exam was repaired after reading
the arms' answers, so the repair is judged only on scenarios rendered after it (new seeds) and on the child-authored
set, never on the runs that prompted it.

## Lenses (pack: fitted + required + invented)
- Required: **inversion** (how initiative fails: floods the inbox, "fixes" what was intended, files Foreman's own setup
  faults as the user's bugs, proves a bug with a test that fails for the wrong reason, scouts a repo the user doesn't
  own); **sci-fi** (the 2030 night shift that hands over a ranked list of proven, fixed defects each morning, worked
  back to deterministic finders + a test judge today); **self-modification** (finders scored on outcomes and muted
  under a precision floor; probe edits gated on a held-out exam).
- Invented: **planted-defect exam** (every finder is measured on renders with known defects and on clean twins before
  it touches a user repo); **false-alarm economics** (an unasked finding costs the user's attention: price it, cap it,
  prove it); **night shift** (what runs unattended between sessions, with what budget and what it may touch).
- Fitted: user value, reliability, simplicity, bold bets, blind spots.

## Gaps this Mission targets (gap map #1; planned briefs, open until the exam shows them closed)
| Gap | Tier | Brief |
|---|---|---|
| The exam punishes true findings: latent base-app defects and a broken README command | 3 | 1 |
| Finders: language-agnostic, deterministic, zero on clean | 3 | 2 |
| find → prove → fix pipeline: a finding is reported only with a red-for-the-right-reason proof | 4 | 3, 4 |
| Project scout: probes over user projects, capped and proven, Foreman's own faults routed to the self-inbox | 3 | 5 |
| Value ranking: severity × proof × reach ÷ effort, per-finder precision from outcomes | 3 | 6 |
| No held-out, child-authored exam for #1 (multi-defect, no request, clean twins) | 3 | 7 |
| Ecosystems + scout on fm code, MCP, site, pane | 3 | 8 |

## Approaches
A. **Chosen — finders propose, a test judges.** Deterministic finders (and later a model finder) emit candidates; a
   candidate becomes a finding only when the prove gate gives it a proof ticket: a test that is red on the untouched
   tree for an assertion reason, red 3 runs of 3, and green once the defect's line is reverted or fixed. Unproven
   candidates are leads (kept, never shown as findings). The gate shows the candidate's line makes a check fail, not
   that the check tests what the user wanted, so the precision it buys is the exam's false-alarm column to show on
   held-out scenarios, not assumed; recall is the finders' job.
B. A better prompt for a model-only finder (the session arms today). Not the primary: the arms already find 3/3 and
   lose on precision; kept as a feeder into A's gate (brief 4 runs it as one finder).
C. Per-language static analysers (semgrep, clippy, eslint, bandit). Not now: each needs an install (that's #5) and
   is one language; the finder interface takes adapters later (captured to Mission 6, tools).
D. Prosecutor and defender agents per finding. A spike (cold refuter): if a defender that can't refute a proven
   finding adds no precision over the proof gate, it isn't built.

## Design
1. **Exam contract repair** (tier 3). README run command `shlex.join(build.split()) + " && ./t"` (the `&&` unquoted);
   the README states the edge contract every language's clean app follows: page n < 1 or size < 1 is empty, clamp
   with lo > hi returns lo, label writes at most `width` columns plus the string and the C one takes a capacity,
   dedupe takes any long (no index by value), total of nothing is 0. Hidden edge tests for each clause run on the
   clean render in all six languages (exam of the exam). The grading rule (T-2120; it moves no exam
   score until a run exercises it): an unkeyed finding whose test fails
   on the clean base and passes on the arm's tree is an **exam defect** (counted, logged, not a false alarm); without
   one, it stays a false alarm. Limit: that test is the arm's own, so an arm can move its own finding out of the
   false-alarm column with a test that asserts its own change. T-2170 makes an outside check decide (the finding
   must break a README edge-contract clause whose hidden test fails on clean); until then exam_defects is read
   beside false_alarms, never as a precision gain, and since the proof gate (brief 3) writes exactly that kind of test,
   no #1 score subtracts exam defects from false alarms before T-2170.
   Re-run the oracle, empty and finders arms; the oracle stays 100%.
2. **`fm find [PATH] [--json]`** (tier 3, new fmfind.py). Deterministic, language-agnostic finders over a tree, each a
   function returning candidates `{finder, kind, file, symbol, line, says, probe}`: untested (a public function no
   test names), docs (fmdocs.scan), deps (an import of a package no manifest declares and the stdlib doesn't have,
   fmoutside.dependencies), sql (a query string built by concatenation or interpolation of a parameter), slow (a
   membership test on a list inside a loop over the input), flaky (random/time in a test with no seed), secrets
   (fmsecrets._tree), failing gates (fm adopt's gate run, rerun once: flaky vs fail). Generated and vendored paths are
   fenced out (fmmap's fences). Every finder reports 0 on every clean exam render; recall per finder is measured on the
   planted ones. The exam's finders arm becomes `fm find`.
3. **Prove gate — `fm find prove ID|--all`** (tier 4). For each candidate a proof ticket: the finder's probe or a
   model-written test (tool-less model call with the candidate, the file and the test style; the test runs with
   fmbench.CREDENTIALS stripped) is run on a copy of the untouched tree; the ticket holds the command, exit, the
   failing assertion line and three runs. It is **proven** when red 3/3 for an assertion (not an import, setup, syntax
   or timeout error: classified by the failure text) and green once the candidate's hunk is reverted or the fix
   lands (mutate-to-confirm, through `fm task prove`'s machinery). Kinds a test can't judge (docs drift, an
   undeclared dep, a credential) prove by their own check re-run cold. Unproven → `leads.jsonl`, never an inbox item.
4. **Initiative pipeline + `/foreman:initiative` skill** (tier 4). `fm find --fix` and the skill, for no request or
   "make this great": map (fmmap) → find → prove → rank (brief 6) → one task per proven finding, fixed test-first on
   a lane (`fm run` lanes, PARALLEL_MAX); the proof test is the task's red; the fix's revert must flip it red again.
   A "clean" verdict is first class: a receipt of what ran and found nothing. The model finder (approach B) is one
   finder here, its candidates through the same gate.
5. **Project scout probes** (tier 3). `probe_find` in fmscout runs `fm find` + prove on the user's own project
   (registered and git-owned by the user's identity; else refused), at most 3 captures a day, proven only, each with
   its proof ticket. probe_doctor's failures in a user project go to Foreman's self-inbox, not the project (the gap
   map's "Noticed"). A refutation ledger: a dismissed or reverted finding's fingerprint (finder, file, symbol, says
   normalised) is never filed again.
6. **Value ranking** (tier 3). `fm find --rank`: score = severity (kind weight) × proof strength (proven 1, lead 0.2)
   × reach (callers from fmgraph, hot files) ÷ effort (hunk size); per-finder precision from fm outcomes (kept vs
   dismissed/reverted, prior 0.5 over 10 cases) multiplies in, and a finder under a 0.3 floor is muted with a line in
   `fm find` saying so. Abstains (no capture) below a threshold. The order is what scout captures and the pipeline fixes.

Parent: gen-0.md (read it; this Seed never overrides a MUST or NEVER there). Inputs: gap-map.md (13 recon passes at

and none decides done): Foreman's finders arm found 90/108 planted defects on s0-001 (30/36 held out, 0 false alarms)

9/18, plain found 6/18 with 6 false alarms and fixed 11/18. That is the baseline the next Seed beats, and it says Foreman's
session arm doesn't yet beat plain.

## What this generation is for
Gen 0's cross-cutting finding is that Foreman *advises* and stops: the parts exist, the trigger and the closed loop
don't. Every Mission below is judged by one question: after it, does Foreman **act** on its own, in a repo it has
never seen, and **prove** it, where before it printed a hint? A Mission that only adds a report is tier 1–2 and goes
to the inbox.

## Standing rules (user steers, recorded with fm decide; every later Seed and Mission carries them)
1. **No idea is killed for ambition.** A failed spike gets at least two genuinely different approaches (different
   mechanism, not a retuned parameter). If all fail, the idea goes to `not-yet.md` (`fm genesis put not-yet.md`) with
   what blocked it, the approaches tried and the capability that would unblock it — never dropped. Every Seed re-reads
   not-yet.md and retries each item whose blocker a capability built since may have removed. Only proven harm or an
   exact duplicate removes an idea for good, and the reason is recorded in not-yet.md's "Removed" section.
2. **Coverage by grid, not by luck.** `coverage.md` rows are every capability area: the 13 of gen-0 §2 plus everything
   a best-in-class agent harness and Claude Code plugin could do, including onboarding, UX, docs, ecosystem,
   multi-user, observability, security, performance, portability. Columns are every surface (Claude Code, fm code,
   other agents, MCP, Desktop, site, CLI, headless/server) × every stage (find, understand, plan, build, verify, ship,
   operate, learn). Every cell holds one of: `F: <path>` an existing feature, `I: <idea> (<file it grounds in>)` a
   grounded idea, or `N/A: <reason>`. Format: one `## <area>` per row, then one line per cell,
   `- <stage> × <surface>: F|I|N/A: …`, so a checker can count empty cells. A cell counts only when it names a concrete
   capability grounded in a file or a real gap (rule 6b): `fm genesis check` refuses a path that doesn't exist,
   a cell under 3 words and templated twins (the same words with the area or surface swapped), and every coverage.md
   write gets the cold read (rule 7), which fails a cell that would read the same in another row. Every generation fills empty
   cells first.
3. **Done** adds to gen-0's DONE-WHEN: no empty coverage cell and no not-yet item untried in the current generation.
4. Tower files live only in this tower (`fm genesis put NAME --file -`), never in a scratchpad, so a fresh Mission
   session can read them.
5. **Weakness-finding uses signals Foreman didn't author.** Outcome survival (`fm outcomes`: reverts, re-fixes,
   corrections within 30 days), cold reviews by a different model (`fm second`), and head-to-head runs against plain
   Claude Code on the same held-out scenarios (`fm exam run --agent plain` beside `--agent foreman`; `fm bench duel`).
   Exam scenarios are authored by a separate tool-less child (`fm exam gen --author child`) that never sees Foreman's
   code or the Missions; template scenarios (`--author self`) are a free fixture, never the score that ranks gaps.
   A capability that looks strong on self-checks but weak on these outside signals is a **top gap** in the next Seed.
6. **Proof only where it decides** (the user's testing-cadence steer, 2026-10-29). (a) Always: red-first unit tests,
   `fm check` and `fm task finish` audits. Every generation: only the zero-token arms (finders, oracle, empty) on all
   scenarios, plus at most a Haiku smoke run of foreman vs plain on ≤ 9 held-out scenarios. Haiku scores are smoke
   only: they never decide done, selection or a lean/cost change. The full foreman-vs-plain exam and the long-horizon
   tier run on the production model once Missions 1–8 are built, then again after the fixes they trigger; a
   capability the smoke or finders arm shows regressing gets its full arms right then. (b) Coverage is real: rule 2.
   (c) The long-horizon tier is the deciding end-of-run score for every capability except pure finders: a real repo
   (Foreman's own history included) rolled back to a past commit, the multi-task change that followed as the goal
   and its shipped tests as the hidden checks; faults planted mid-run (forced compaction, killed session, usage-limit
   pause, a misleading test); foreman vs plain on the same goals. Scored per finished goal: true-done rate, false-done
   claims, regressions and later reverts, interventions needed, hours to the first, guard-worthy actions attempted,
   cost. Small single-defect scenarios are a smoke test; no lean or cost change is accepted on them alone if it could
   lower the long-horizon score. (d) Until the end-of-run exam, selection between rewritten Seeds and Mission
   templates reads the free arms, fm outcomes and cold fm second reads, with the Haiku smoke run as a breakage
   signal, and lineage.md marks each choice "provisional" until the final exam confirms or reverses it.
7. **Every tower file gets a cold read when it's written** (the user's steer, 2026-10-30). Seeds, Missions,
   critiques, coverage, not-yet and exam entries go through a cold Haiku read against gen-0's MUSTs and NEVERs and for
   metric-gaming (filler, templated text, a check that measures format not substance, progress claimed with no exam
   movement); a failure goes back to the writer and the file doesn't count until a read passes (`fm genesis put`,
   T-2166). Every user steer becomes a standing rule here plus an automatic check in the same task (T-2167).
A user grant (the push-to-main one of 2026-10-29) is not a rule here: a steer only adds to gen-0, so grants live in
